title: Beginning Level Carolina Shag Dance Lesson 1

observation_window.sampling: provider default; not continuous motion capture

extraction.teacher_style: The instructors present a clear, structured breakdown of the steps while standing side-by-side in front of the camera. They alternate speaking roles to explain both partner roles, frame, and rhythm details.

lesson_structure.note: Introduction of Todd and Louise Dickson and overview of Carolina Shag
Explanation of slot dancing, handholds, tension, and posture
Demonstration of basic and turning shag steps to music
Detailed breakdown of the basic step counts and footwork
Explanation and demonstration of the female underarm turn

cues: Keep your knees flexible not stiff
Weight forward on the balls of your feet
Start a new step on count 1
metaphors: Imagine being on a diving board
Shag is a smooth version of swing
common_mistakes: Getting the partner out of alignment and balance during turns
safety: Do not press hard on the hand connection because that can hurt

steps_taught.name: The Basic
steps_taught.description: Triple step, triple step, rock step in a slot

steps_taught.name: Female Under Arm Turn
steps_taught.description: Basic step with the female turning under the raised lead hand

what_works: Clear verbal distinction between leader and follower footwork
Repetitive counts and verbal guidance during demonstrations
what_hinders: Lack of slow-tempo breakdown without music

quotes.text: Shag is more than just the dance steps.

evidence_segments.observation: Both teachers stand facing the camera with neutral posture while introducing the dance history and social aspects.
Female teacher demonstrates handholds while male teacher explains hand positioning and finger placement.
Couple dances together to music with exaggerated step sizes and smooth gliding motion.

extraction.distinctive_method: Instructors explicitly use spatial imagery like a diving board and a slot to teach floorcraft and alignment before introducing footwork.
